A man was prosecuted for assault and battery after he admitted striking a victim with a pool cue during a barroom argument. The man claimed that he acted in self-defense after he was attacked by the victim, who was drunk and belligerent. As his first defense witness, the man calls his neighbor to testify that the man is a good neighbor. The neighbor's testimony is
Option A: admissible, because it is relevant to show the improbability of the man's having committed an unprovoked attack.
Option B: admissible, because it is relevant to support the man's credibility.
Option C: inadmissible, because it is merely the opinion of a character witness.
Option D: inadmissible, because it is not directed toward a pertinent trait of the man's character.
